The multiples of $10$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
C=\{10,20,30,40,50,60,70,…\}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $5$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
D=\{5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45,50,55,60,65,70,75,…\}.
$$

Now, $C∖D$ is the *difference* of $C$ and $D,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $C$ but *not* in $D.$

The elements of $C$ that are also in $D$ are $10,20,30,40,$ and so on (i.e. multiples of $10$). So, we must remove these elements from $C.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}C∖D & =C-D \\  & =\{10,20,30,40,50,60,70,…\}-\{5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45,50,55,60,65,70,75,…\} \\  & =∅.\end{aligned}
$$
